test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: 11 men and 17 women can complete a piece of work in 6 days, and 18 men and 15 women can complete the same work in 4 days. The work of how many women is equivalent to that of one man?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equate total work: (11M + 17W) × 6 = (18M + 15W) × 4

Divide both sides by 2: 3(11M + 17W) = 2(18M + 15W)

Expand terms: 33M + 51W = 36M + 30W

Rearrange like terms: 36M − 33M = 51W − 30W

3M = 21W ⇒ 1M = 7W

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: 11 men and 17 women in 6 days | 18 men and 15 women in 4 days

Formula Used: Total Work = Efficiency × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b6a641ef7227ab3951feb01a687eccc05acb983d94e26eb5c80df8da117fe4d2.png] 

Let efficiency of 1 man be M and 1 woman be W.

⇒ Total Work = (11M + 17W) × 6

⇒ Total Work = (18M + 15W) × 4

⇒ 6(11M + 17W) = 4(18M + 15W)

⇒ 66M + 102W = 72M + 60W

⇒ 72M − 66M = 102W − 60W

⇒ 6M = 42W

⇒ 1M = 7W

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Man-Day Formula

For group work, M₁D₁H₁/W₁ = M₂D₂H₂/W₂, where M is number of people, D is days, H is hours, and W is work done.

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the work (E ∝ 1/T).

Work Equivalence

When different groups complete the same work, their total man-days must be equated to find individual efficiency ratios.
